Antisemitism. This systematic prejudice against Jews has roots in medieval Christian Europe, where theology held Jews collectively responsible for the death of Jesus, leading to centuries of legal discrimination. Expulsions from Spain, England, and France followed periods of violent pogroms. Nineteenth-century racial pseudoscience reimagined Jews as a racial threat, and emancipation actually intensified this hatred among those fearing Jewish economic power. Nazi Germany weaponized antisemitism as state policy, resulting in the Holocaust and the murder of roughly six million Jews.
